## README.md
# public-coastal — Coastal Datasets

Global datasets describing the coastline and the coastal zone.

## Ecological Coastal Units (`ecu`)

The world's ocean coastline divided into 4,005,842 segments of 1 km or shorter (median about 480 m). Each segment is described by ten variables covering the adjacent water, the adjacent land and the shoreline itself. Produced by the U.S. Geological Survey with Esri and the Marine Biodiversity Observation Network.

- The segments follow a 30 m global shoreline traced from **2014** Landsat imagery. That makes this a snapshot of the 2014 coastline: useful for describing coastal settings, not for measuring recent shoreline change.
- Each segment has measured values (wave height, tidal range, chlorophyll, turbidity, sinuosity, slope, river outflow, erodibility, climate regime, marine physical environment) and a class label for each.
- The ten class labels together define a **coastal segment unit** (`CSU_ID`, 80,997 distinct), following the Coastal and Marine Ecological Classification Standard (CMECS). Units are grouped into 16 global coastline groups (`Cluster`), which the source numbers but does not name.
- `REGIONAL_SINUOSITY = 0` (591,757 segments) means no value was computed; exclude it before averaging.

| Asset | URL |
|---|---|
| GeoParquet | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/ecu.parquet` |
| PMTiles | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/ecu.pmtiles` (source layer **`ecu`**) |
| H3 hex (resolution 8) | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/ecu/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet` |
| STAC | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/ecu/stac-collection.json` |

The H3 hex table has one row per (segment, cell) pair, so deduplicate on `_cng_fid` before summing `LENGTH_GEO`.

### DuckDB

```sql
INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial;
-- coastline length by tidal class, in km
SELECT tidal_label, SUM(LENGTH_GEO) / 1000 AS coast_km, COUNT(*) AS segments
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/ecu.parquet')
GROUP BY tidal_label
ORDER BY coast_km DESC;
```

### MapLibre GL JS

The PMTiles `source-layer` is **`ecu`**.

```js
import { Protocol } from "pmtiles";
maplibregl.addProtocol("pmtiles", new Protocol().tile);

map.addSource("ecu", {
  type: "vector",
  url: "pmtiles://https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/ecu.pmtiles",
});
map.addLayer({
  id: "ecu-tidal",
  type: "line",
  source: "ecu",
  "source-layer": "ecu",
  paint: {
    "line-width": 2,
    "line-color": [
      "match", ["get", "tidal_label"],
      "atidal", "#d4e6f1", "microtidal", "#a9cce3", "minimally tidal", "#7fb3d5",
      "moderately tidal", "#5499c7", "macrotidal", "#2471a3", "megatidal", "#1a5276",
      "#999999",
    ],
  },
});
```

### Source and licence

Sayre, R., 2023, *Global Ecological Classification of Coastal Segment Units*, U.S. Geological Survey data release, https://doi.org/10.5066/P9HWHSPU. Method: Sayre et al. 2021, *Oceanography* 34(2), https://doi.org/10.5670/oceanog.2021.219.

Public domain (U.S. Government work). Retrieved from ScienceBase on 2026-09-28; the original package is kept at `s3://public-coastal/raw/USGSEsriGlobalCoastalSegmentsv1.mpk` (2,075,928,715 bytes, MD5 `ad4f54e071c343ccbd574f4cff0adf36`).

## MEOW Coastal Band (`meow-coastal-band`)

A coastal strip labelled with Marine Ecoregions of the World (MEOW) ecoregion, province and realm: everything within 50 km of the coastline on the sea side and 20 km on the land side. MEOW ecoregion polygons reach far inland and about 200 nautical miles out to sea, so this band is the coastal part of each ecoregion. It comes in two forms:

- **H3 hex table** — one row per H3 resolution 8 cell, with distance to the coast (`dist_km`), sea or land (`side`), depth or elevation. Use it for joins with other H3 layers and for choosing any strip width.
- **Polygons** (GeoParquet and PMTiles) — the same cells merged into one multipolygon per ecoregion, side and distance class: sea 0–5, 5–10, 10–20 and 20–50 km; land 0–5, 5–10 and 10–20 km. There are 1,462 features, each with `ECO_CODE`, `ECOREGION`, `PROVINCE`, `REALM`, `side`, `dist_min_km`, `dist_max_km` and `area_km2`. Each class includes its upper edge, so keeping features with `dist_max_km <= 10` gives exactly the cells with `dist_km <= 10`.

| Asset | URL |
|---|---|
| H3 hex (resolution 8) | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/meow-coastal-band/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet` |
| GeoParquet | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/meow-coastal-band.parquet` |
| PMTiles | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/meow-coastal-band.pmtiles` (source layer **`meow-coastal-band`**, zoom 0–10) |
| STAC | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/meow-coastal-band/stac-collection.json` |

### DuckDB

```sql
-- sea area within 10 km of the coast, per realm, in km2
SELECT REALM, SUM(area_km2) AS sea_km2
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/meow-coastal-band.parquet')
WHERE side = 'sea' AND dist_max_km <= 10
GROUP BY REALM ORDER BY sea_km2 DESC;
```

### MapLibre GL JS

The PMTiles `source-layer` is **`meow-coastal-band`**.

```js
import { Protocol } from "pmtiles";
maplibregl.addProtocol("pmtiles", new Protocol().tile);

map.addSource("meow-band", {
  type: "vector",
  url: "pmtiles://https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/meow-coastal-band.pmtiles",
});
map.addLayer({
  id: "meow-band-sea-10km",
  type: "fill",
  source: "meow-band",
  "source-layer": "meow-coastal-band",
  filter: ["all", ["==", ["get", "side"], "sea"], ["<=", ["get", "dist_max_km"], 10]],
  paint: {
    "fill-color": ["match", ["get", "dist_max_km"], 5, "#08519c", 10, "#6baed6", "#c6dbef"],
    "fill-opacity": 0.8,
  },
});
```

### Source and licence

Derived from MEOW (Spalding et al. 2007; The Nature Conservancy / WWF, CC-BY-NC-3.0), so it carries MEOW's NonCommercial terms. The coastline is the USGS Ecological Coastal Units shoreline (above); land and sea come from the Copernicus GLO-90 Water Body Mask, depth from GEBCO 2025 and elevation from Copernicus DEM GLO-90 (produced using Copernicus WorldDEM-90 © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA).

## Global tidal marshes 2020 (`tidal-marsh-2020`)

Tidal marshes, the vegetated coastal wetlands flooded by the tides, mapped for 2020 at 10 m between 60 degrees north and 60 degrees south (Worthington et al. 2024, version 2.6).

- Global total in this collection: **52,876 km2**, against the producers' published 52,880 km2 (95% confidence interval 32,030 to 59,780).
- Raster values: 1 = tidal marsh, 0 = mapped but not tidal marsh, 255 = outside the producers' tiles.
- The H3 table has one row per resolution 8 cell holding any tidal marsh, with `tidal_marsh_km2` and `tidal_marsh_fraction`; a missing cell means zero.

| Asset | URL |
|---|---|
| COG (10 m) | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/tidal-marsh-2020/tidal-marsh-2020-cog.tif` |
| H3 hex (resolution 8) | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/tidal-marsh-2020/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet` |
| STAC | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/tidal-marsh-2020/stac-collection.json` |

### DuckDB

```sql
-- tidal marsh area, in km2, per MEOW coastal ecoregion
SELECT b.ECOREGION, SUM(t.tidal_marsh_km2) AS marsh_km2
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/tidal-marsh-2020/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet') t
JOIN read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/meow-coastal-band/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet') b USING (h8, h0)
GROUP BY b.ECOREGION ORDER BY marsh_km2 DESC;
```

### MapLibre GL JS

The rasters render through the NRP titiler service; the colormap draws value 1 and leaves 0 and 255 transparent.

```js
map.addSource("tidal-marsh-2020", {
  type: "raster",
  tiles: ["https://titiler.nrp-nautilus.io/cog/tiles/WebMercatorQuad/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?url=https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/tidal-marsh-2020/tidal-marsh-2020-cog.tif&colormap=%7B%220%22%3A%5B0%2C0%2C0%2C0%5D%2C%221%22%3A%5B44%2C127%2C184%2C255%5D%2C%22255%22%3A%5B0%2C0%2C0%2C0%5D%7D"],
  tileSize: 256,
});
map.addLayer({ id: "tidal-marsh-2020", type: "raster", source: "tidal-marsh-2020" });
```

### Source and licence

Worthington, T. A., Spalding, M., Landis, E., Maxwell, T. L., Navarro, A., Smart, L. S., & Murray, N. J. (2024). The distribution of global tidal marshes from Earth observation data. *Global Ecology and Biogeography*, 33(8), e13852, https://doi.org/10.1111/geb.13852. Data: Zenodo record 8420753, version 2.6, downloaded 2026-10-25; the original archive is kept at `s3://public-coastal/raw/tidal-marsh-2020/tidal_marsh_v2_6.zip`.

Creative Commons Attribution 4.0.

## Global tidal flats (`tidal-flats-v1-2`, `tidal-flats-v1-1`)

Tidal flats, the mud, sand and rock flats exposed at low tide, mapped at 30 m for three-year periods between 60 degrees north and 60 degrees south (Murray et al.). Two collections, because the producers' two versions use different mapped areas and should not be joined into one series:

- **`tidal-flats-v1-2`**: version 1.2, seven periods from 1999-2001 to 2017-2019.
- **`tidal-flats-v1-1`**: version 1.1, the five periods from 1984-1986 to 1996-1998 that version 1.2 does not cover, plus the version 1.1 mapped-area layer (`datamask`).

Raster values: 1 = tidal flat, 0 = not tidal flat or outside the mapped area. The H3 tables have one row per (period, resolution 8 cell) holding any tidal flat, with `epoch`, `tidal_flat_km2` and `tidal_flat_fraction`. Totals differ noticeably between periods (the two latest version 1.2 periods are about 30% above 1999-2013); these differences are in the producers' maps, which they caution are not a consistent time series everywhere.

| Asset | URL |
|---|---|
| COG per period (30 m) | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/tidal-flats-v1-2/tidal-flats-<period>-cog.tif`, `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/tidal-flats-v1-1/tidal-flats-<period>-cog.tif` |
| H3 hex (resolution 8) | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/tidal-flats-v1-2/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet`, `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/tidal-flats-v1-1/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet` |
| Mapped area, version 1.1 | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/tidal-flats-v1-1/datamask-cog.tif`, `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/tidal-flats-v1-1/datamask/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet` |
| STAC | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/tidal-flats-v1-2/stac-collection.json`, `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/tidal-flats-v1-1/stac-collection.json` |

### DuckDB

```sql
-- tidal flat area per period, in km2
SELECT epoch, SUM(tidal_flat_km2) AS km2
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/tidal-flats-v1-2/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet')
GROUP BY epoch ORDER BY epoch;
```

The rasters render through the NRP titiler service; the colormap draws value 1 and leaves 0 and 255 transparent.

```js

  tiles: ["https://titiler.nrp-nautilus.io/cog/tiles/WebMercatorQuad/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?url=https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/tidal-flats-v1-2/tidal-flats-2017-2019-cog.tif&colormap=%7B%220%22%3A%5B0%2C0%2C0%2C0%5D%2C%221%22%3A%5B194%2C163%2C90%2C255%5D%2C%22255%22%3A%5B0%2C0%2C0%2C0%5D%7D"],

## Global coastal typology (`coastal-typology-durr-2011`)

A global classification of the coast into geomorphic types that describe how a stretch of coast filters what rivers carry to the sea (Dürr et al. 2011). Two layers share the class column `FIN_TYP`:

- **`coastline`**: 9,604 line segments drawn along the edges of a 0.5-degree grid. Segments can lie up to about 25 km from the true shoreline.
- **`catchments`**: 7,057 polygons of the land draining to each stretch of coast, built from the STN-30 version 6 river basins. A basin can span several polygons, so total `BASINAREA` over distinct `BASINID`.

`FIN_TYP` values: 0 endorheic or glaciated, 1 small deltas, 2 tidal systems, 3 lagoons, 4 fjords and fjärds, 5 large rivers (Va), 51 large rivers with tidal deltas (Vb, catchments only), 6 karst, 7 arheic, -9999 no data (catchments only). On the coastline layer, code 5 covers both large-river subtypes.

| Asset | URL |
|---|---|
| GeoParquet | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/coastal-typology-durr-2011/coastline.parquet`, `.../catchments.parquet` |
| PMTiles | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/coastal-typology-durr-2011/coastline.pmtiles` (source layer **`coastline`**), `.../catchments.pmtiles` (source layer **`catchments`**) |
| H3 hex (resolution 8) | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/coastal-typology-durr-2011/coastline/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet`, `.../catchments/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet` |
| STAC | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/coastal-typology-durr-2011/stac-collection.json` |

The H3 hex tables have one row per (feature, cell) pair, so deduplicate on `_cng_fid` before counting features.

### DuckDB

```sql
-- coastline segments of each type
SELECT FIN_TYP, COUNT(*) AS segments
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/coastal-typology-durr-2011/coastline.parquet')
GROUP BY FIN_TYP
ORDER BY FIN_TYP;
```

### MapLibre GL JS

The PMTiles `source-layer` is **`catchments`** (or **`coastline`** for the line layer).

```js

maplibregl.addProtocol("pmtiles", new Protocol().tile);

map.addSource("coastal-typology", {
  type: "vector",

});

  id: "coastal-typology-catchments",
  type: "fill",
  source: "coastal-typology",
  "source-layer": "catchments",
  paint: {
    "fill-opacity": 0.7,
    "fill-color": [
      "match", ["get", "FIN_TYP"],
      0, "#c7dccb", 1, "#8c5a3c", 2, "#e31a1c", 3, "#33cc33", 4, "#1f3fbf",

### Source and licence

## Global mangrove typology version 3 (`mangrove-typology-v3`)

A global classification of the world's mangroves by the coastal setting they grow in (Worthington et al.). Mangrove patches are grouped into 3,983 geomorphic units, each classed as `Delta`, `Estuary`, `Lagoon` or `OpenCoast` in the `Class` column. The typology is matched to the Global Mangrove Watch version 3.12 extent.

There are twelve layers with the same units and classes: `composite` (every year's extent combined) and one layer per mapped year (`1996`, `2007`, `2008`, `2009`, `2010`, `2015`, `2016`, `2017`, `2018`, `2019`, `2020`). A unit keeps its `Type` (for example `Delta_30028`) and `ID` in every layer, so use either to match units across years. `OGC_FID` differs between layers. In the 1996 layer two units, `Lagoon_8338` and `Lagoon_8440`, are each split across two rows, so count units over distinct `Type`.

| Asset | URL |
|---|---|
| GeoParquet | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/mangrove-typology-v3/<layer>.parquet` |
| PMTiles | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/mangrove-typology-v3/<layer>.pmtiles` (source layer = the layer name, for example **`2020`**) |
| H3 hex (resolution 8) | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/mangrove-typology-v3/<layer>/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet` |
| STAC | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/mangrove-typology-v3/stac-collection.json` |

The H3 hex tables have one row per (unit, cell) pair. A cell belongs to a unit when its centre lies inside the unit's mangroves, or, for a patch too small to hold a cell centre, when it holds a point inside the patch. Use the hexagons to locate units and the polygons for mangrove area.

### DuckDB

```sql
-- units of each class in 2020
SELECT Class, COUNT(DISTINCT Type) AS units
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/mangrove-typology-v3/2020.parquet')
GROUP BY Class
ORDER BY Class;
```

### MapLibre GL JS

The PMTiles `source-layer` is the layer name, for example **`2020`** or **`composite`**.

```js
import { Protocol } from "pmtiles";
maplibregl.addProtocol("pmtiles", new Protocol().tile);

map.addSource("mangrove-typology", {
  type: "vector",
  url: "pmtiles://https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/mangrove-typology-v3/2020.pmtiles",
});
map.addLayer({
  id: "mangrove-typology-2020",
  type: "fill",
  source: "mangrove-typology",
  "source-layer": "2020",
  paint: {
    "fill-opacity": 0.8,
    "fill-color": [
      "match", ["get", "Class"],
      "Delta", "#8c5a3c", "Estuary", "#1f78b4", "Lagoon", "#33a02c", "OpenCoast", "#ff7f00",

A global biophysical typology of mangroves and its relevance for ecosystem structure and deforestation. *Scientific Reports* 10, 14652, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-020-71194-5. Data downloaded from Zenodo on 2026-11-03.


## IPCC AR6 sea-level projections (`ar6-sea-level-projections`)

Projections of relative sea-level change from the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (Working Group I, chapter 9), version 20210809, at 1,030 tide gauges and 65,160 nodes of a 1-degree global grid. Change is in millimetres since the 1995-2014 baseline and rates in millimetres per year, from 2020 to 2150 under five SSP emissions scenarios and five warming levels, and to 2300 for the low-confidence projections. Each projection carries 107 quantiles (`p0` to `p100`; `p0_1` is the 0.1st percentile, `p99_5` the 99.5th) for the total and for each contributing process.

- **`regional-confidence`**: relative sea level including vertical land motion, as a coastal location experiences it.
- **`regional-confidence-novlm`**: the same without vertical land motion and other background processes.
- **`coastal-band/hex`**: every H3 resolution-8 cell of the MEOW coastal band (`meow-coastal-band`), with the with-VLM total change of the nearest grid node that has a projection in every year of each scenario (p5, p17, p50, p83, p95). This is a nearest-node assignment, not an interpolation; `location_id` names the node. The node is usually within 40 km of the cell (99% within about 70 km). In the 5 °C warming level (`tlim5.0win0.25`), upstream has projections at only 2 of the 83 Black Sea grid nodes, so most of the Black Sea coast takes values from nodes outside the sea, up to 982 km away.

The tables have one row per location, scenario, confidence level, component, measure and year, so filter on all of them to get one projection. A missing projection is null in every quantile column.

| Asset | URL |
|---|---|
| GeoParquet (points) | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/ar6-sea-level-projections/regional-confidence.parquet`, `.../regional-confidence-novlm.parquet` |
| H3 hex (resolution 8) | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/ar6-sea-level-projections/coastal-band/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet` |
| STAC | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/ar6-sea-level-projections/stac-collection.json` |

There is no PMTiles layer: the tables are point projections with many rows per location. For a map, draw the hex for one scenario, confidence level and year.

### DuckDB

```sql
-- likely range of sea-level rise in 2100 under SSP2-4.5 at a tide gauge
SELECT location_name, p17, p50, p83
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coastal/ar6-sea-level-projections/regional-confidence.parquet')
WHERE location_name = 'SAN_FRANCISCO' AND component = 'total' AND measure = 'values'
  AND scenario = 'ssp245' AND confidence = 'medium' AND year = 2100;
```

### MapLibre GL JS

There are no vector tiles for this dataset. To map it, query the hex for one scenario, confidence level and year and draw the cells, for example with deck.gl's `H3HexagonLayer`:
